questions.stem: In a right-angled triangle, the hypotenuse is 10 cm and one angle is 30 degrees. What is the length of the side opposite the 30-degree angle?
questions.explanation: O = H x sin(theta) = 10 x sin(30) = 10 x 0.5 = 5 cm.

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has an angle of 55 degrees and the adjacent side is 8 cm. Find the opposite side to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: O = A x tan(theta) = 8 x tan(55) = 8 x 1.4281 = 11.4 cm (1 d.p.).

questions.stem: A ramp rises at 15 degrees to the horizontal. If the vertical height is 1.2 m, how long is the ramp to 1 decimal place?
questions.explanation: The ramp is the hypotenuse. H = O / sin(theta) = 1.2 / sin(15) = 1.2 / 0.2588 = 4.6 m (1 d.p.).

questions.stem: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of 12 cm and an angle of 40 degrees. Find the adjacent side to 1 decimal place.
questions.explanation: A = H x cos(theta) = 12 x cos(40) = 12 x 0.7660 = 9.2 cm (1 d.p.).
